scope: Bounded re-review of previously reported cleanup and run-identity issues; no renewed numerical/operator audit or formal acceptance

checks.finding: try/finally encloses model construction, preparation early return, query, retrieval and generation. It closes live models, clears model/bound-method references, runs GC and empties the CUDA cache. Normal E-to-G release remains before G construction.
close explicitly sets num.failure_callback=None, clears weights/KV cache and releases progress callback; this breaks the _begin report closure back-reference.
Once construction succeeds, try/finally covers model arithmetic, synchronization, record/vector writes and printing; finally calls close, deletes the model reference and empties the cache.

Snapshot binds entrypoint, helper, local input source, reference sources, numeric profile/constants/evidence, template, both quantized manifests, checkpoint manifests and actual tokenizer/config files. Loaded quantized weights retain their existing per-file manifest checks.

Both entrypoints capture before model/operator execution and record the start-to-finish identity comparison. The constants and checker-script provenance omissions identified in the previous review are covered.

Full runner persists the start identity before run_reference and checks identity again on the ordinary exception-record and normal-result paths. The comparison is an explicit boolean in the record; a false value must not be treated as a same-identity completed result.

boundaries: Static cleanup coverage was checked, but this review did not inject model/CUDA failures or remeasure GPU memory reclamation.

Before/after hashes identify files on disk at the two capture points; they are not an attestation of already-imported Python bytecode and cannot detect a file changed then restored between captures. The frozen-source run discipline remains relevant.
No new full-model, CUDA arithmetic, performance, privacy or R2 correctness claim is made by this review.
